name: Loop
tagline: Arrange Mac windows through a customizable radial menu.
description:
Loop is an open-source Mac window manager built around a radial menu. Press its trigger key, point toward a layout, and release to move the active window into place. The gesture makes common positions easy to remember without assigning a separate keyboard shortcut to every layout.

Loop can also be customized with colors, dimensions, and shortcuts for a preferred desktop setup. It is especially useful when windows need to move among halves, corners, or displays throughout the day.

## Features

- Choose a window position from a radial menu triggered by a key press.
- Move, resize, and arrange windows in repeatable screen regions.
- Customize layouts, colors, keyboard controls, and related window behavior.
- Use the open-source Mac app without creating an account.

## Where it fits

Loop suits people who want fast, gesture-like window placement with visual feedback. It offers a different interaction from simple edge snapping or a list of fixed menu commands, so it may take a short period to build muscle memory.

## Privacy and requirements

Loop needs macOS Accessibility permission to control other application windows. The official project lists macOS 13 or later. Window movement happens locally; granting Accessibility access should still be treated as a system-level permission.

## Pricing

Loop is free and open source; the developer accepts optional sponsorship.
